name: Oral Antibiotics (Doxycycline / Minocycline)
summary: Meant to be a time-limited bridge to a topical-maintenance regimen — not a long-term solution, however comfortable it feels once it’s working.
good: A defined, capped course (commonly a few months) as a bridge to topical maintenance therapy.
bad: Combining with isotretinoin (absolute contraindication), dosing alongside calcium/iron/antacids, or open-ended courses beyond about 3–4 months.
clinicalPearls: Guidelines increasingly cap oral antibiotic courses for acne at a few months specifically because indefinite use offers diminishing benefit while accumulating resistance and side-effect risk.
mechanism: Antibacterial against C. acnes plus a genuinely separate anti-inflammatory effect — inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases and neutrophil chemotaxis — which is why sub-antimicrobial dosing is sometimes used specifically for the anti-inflammatory effect alone.
originalFields: Antibacterial against C. acnes plus a genuinely separate anti-inflammatory effect — inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases and neutrophil chemotaxis — which is why sub-antimicrobial dosing is sometimes used specifically for the anti-inflammatory effect alone.
Moderate-severe inflammatory acne not adequately controlled by topicals alone, used as a bridge rather than indefinite maintenance.
Moderate — 6–8 weeks for meaningful inflammatory improvement.
Systemic rather than topical — photosensitivity (especially doxycycline), GI upset, and minocycline-specific dizziness/vestibular symptoms.
Minocycline carries a rare but recognized risk of blue-gray skin or mucosal pigmentation with prolonged use — distinct from acne-related PIH, but worth knowing given this section’s focus.
No direct topical barrier effect, though photosensitivity increases UV vulnerability.
Not applicable — oral medication, taken away from dairy, calcium, iron, or antacids, which chelate the drug and reduce absorption.
Per prescriber, with a full glass of water and away from meals containing calcium-rich dairy or iron/antacids.
Should be paired with topical benzoyl peroxide to reduce resistance risk; absolutely contraindicated alongside isotretinoin.
